description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Service-level submit_seal admission covers genesis completeness, current device generation, recomputed roots, predecessor notary authority and non-terminal future-clock deferral.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated at the Event CBA basis; linear archive uses the revocation freshness window, tombstone and concurrent archive fail closed immediately, and restore never rehabilitates a pre-archive basis.

Generated limit-1 / limit / limit+1 matrix for MLS Governance Proof response bytes, logical item bytes, chunk count, collection totals, per-chunk item counts, Merkle proof length and chunk request pinning semantics.

Pins strand update/tracks update to data-plane mv_register target_ref routing while stage.set remains control CAS; reducer projections are recomputed from the single causal_refs base head, remain independent of receiver-local current heads, hold on missing dependencies, and reject missing/multiple bases or non-canonical projected post-state with reducer_projection_failed.

Requires every active reducer-input kind to have a complete machine-readable cell contract and pins exact multi-target atomicity, missing/extra reducer-projection rejection, and data/control plane-cross-write rejection.

Binds every durable member-device withheld reason to the unique refusal-policy root and source authorization at the Event CBA/T0 basis; receiver-current, zero, ambiguous, stale, or wrong-scope substitutes fail closed without a terminal projection.

Byte-exact member-device and RRK sender-proof transcripts with omitted inactive branches/material/options; cross-target, double/missing material, field tampering, and sender-device key mismatch fail closed.

Registering an external Organization DID separates resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation; being resolvable or referenceable yields no local administrative authority. prepare/ensure is two-phase by decision: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge bound to purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds, and the control proof binds that beneficiary to block redirection. Challenge consumption atomically records the canonical request digest and outcome, so only a byte-identical retry is idempotent; the same challenge under a different digest fails closed. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs, witness attestation is never a governance quorum, requested scopes MUST match the challenge, and quorum proofs MUST meet the declared threshold. registration_generation reconciles idempotency with terminal revocation: replacement atomically terminates the old current generation and advances a monotonic current pointer, so an old receipt cannot authorize after supersession. Status is the closed triple active/stale/revoked with rotation mapping to stale and DID deactivation forcing revoked, and revoked is terminal against refresh.

did:webvh witness policy is read only from parameters.witness = {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]} with unique did:key ids, and proofs only from the separate did-witness.json keyed by versionId. Malformed, aliased (witnesses / witness_threshold / witnessThreshold), Arkret-overlay-polluted, unavailable, under-threshold, stale or same-controlling-organization evidence all fail closed with a registered code; none of them may degrade to threshold 0. Deployment policy raises but never lowers the method threshold. The fixture includes a field-exact official signed vector that requires entry-hash recomputation plus controller and witness proof verification. Arkret carries observations in ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1, a family distinct from the registry-consensus ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1, returned as a schema-discriminated tagged union that never substitutes for verifying the standard proofs.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.
Managed-agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.

Controller-owned recovery_public_key backup of managed Agent PCR MLS state, canonical managed-principal binding across public/plaintext/AAD views, pairing recovery-readiness gate, and prohibition on Agent runtime private-key backup or per-Agent human mnemonic.

Native Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.
KeyPackage upload, entry upload, consume, and revoke signatures use one byte-exact operation-id domain plus typed unsigned-request JCS transcript shared by ordinary devices and Native Agent runtimes.

Provision requested_scope is a required immutable global ceiling rather than a grant; narrower key scopes and Realm grants are accepted, while action/resource/mandatory-constraint widening fails closed and provisioning emits no Realm grant.

The public managed-Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.

Applet transaction push source signature anchor: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, source_signature_anchor persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/anchor conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.

Realm create is atomically paired with one immediately following closed-form self founding grant for created_by; missing, widened, third-party, reordered, or post-bootstrap replayed founding grants fail closed without leaving a partial Realm or membership.

Hard quota counters use one logical linearizable authority across every service node: a race for the last slot cannot overshoot, idempotent retries count once, unavailable authority fails closed, and calendar-month periods are rejected.

Temporal action gates are neutral for unrelated actions according to effect, while edit/redact windows use the verified target created_at and the fixed verification time/skew to accept inside the deadline and fail closed outside or on missing target time.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).
resolve_agent_selector failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized selectors return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
resolve_handle failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized handles return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
on_last_read converges by principal-level aggregate contributions and read_trigger_window_ms; offline devices receive expiry stubs and shred keys when they reconnect.
Read-trigger expiry anchors are derived from anonymous aggregate contributions and MUST NOT reveal reader identity or reader counts to other clients or services outside the aggregate boundary.
Duplicate, stale, out-of-order, or cross-bound read-trigger contributions MUST NOT refresh anchors, double-count readers, or expire the wrong message.

Opposite delivery orders at two aggregate services converge through per-token and aggregate min joins; a late earlier valid contribution can only move expiry earlier and can never restore shredded content.
BLAKE3 KAT over fixed UTF-8 bytes plus wrong-prefix, wrong-length, Realm-suite mismatch, and unknown-suite downgrade rejection cases.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) raw detached signature golden vector over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind raw_detached_signature; keygen from a recorded xi seed, signature published as a recorded value that verifiers only verify).

Executable signature negative family for Ed25519, ES256, and ML-DSA-65: bad or truncated signatures, alg/key-type mismatch, malformed algorithm-specific public keys, and detached-profile confusion; every case MUST be rejected with the recorded error_code.

Event Batch Receipt events[] is a canonical set projection sorted by UTF8(canonical_json(item)) with duplicates removed before signing; receivers reject unsorted or duplicate signed wire arrays before digest verification.

Hand-written deterministic CBOR bounds: a definite-length array declaring/carrying 65537 items (generator-described, built by the runner) exceeds the v1 cap of 65536 items per array/map and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) without preallocating from the declared count.

CBOR indefinite-length item (raw bytes bf616101ff, the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1}) violates RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_not_deterministic); locks the SDK's existing indefinite-length rejection on the mls_governance_binding decode path.

CBOR capacity bomb: a byte string header declaring 4294967295 bytes with only 4 bytes of remaining input (raw bytes 5affffffffdeadbeef) MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) before any buffer is allocated from the declared length.

Canonical structure depth cap: a JSON object nested 65 levels deep (generator-described, built by the runner; top-level container = depth 1) exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined) and MUST be rejected (reason_code structure_depth_exceeded) with bounded recursion; a depth-64 control input MUST be accepted.

Federation ingress authentication-failure family (unknown peer / not authorized / target absent) returns indistinguishable responses within one timing bucket per relation.md section 4.5 sampling rules.

service_binding_ref.reducer_profile_digest is computed per federation.md section 4.1.1 from a locally rebuilt content-addressed resolved_digest_input closure; event-kind or schema content mutation changes the digest, canonical key reordering does not, and the receiver rejects the whole batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on divergence.

Federation push carries one Realm's minimal receiver-relative, strictly ordered Seal prerequisite closure rooted at DataEvent seal_ref and Control Event seal_basis leaves on the sole peer events rail; receivers resolve Control Events and basis Seals topologically before DataEvents without granting same-batch unsealed authority or advancing actor frontiers.

Ordinary dependency gaps are per-item HTTP 200 partial outcomes while registered founding units remain atomic 503; retry identity changes exactly when the canonical body is reduced after accepted or duplicate items.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_p256_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM, profile-gated interop suite): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.
RFC 8265 human-identifier preparation, canonical-receiver rejection, Unicode localparts and Agent slugs, UTS #46 A-label conversion, and dual code-point/octet limits.
UTS #39 skeleton collision state is scoped to one registration authority and one namespace and never defines canonical equality or wire bytes.

Failure-indistinguishability vector covering both the third-party claim endpoint and the invite-locator resolve endpoint; each endpoint's failure classes MUST share one external response shape and bounded timing distribution.

Realm reducer authority for ak.invite.claim: binding_proof and subject_proof signature transcripts, token_commitment match, verification_service_id allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, pending -> claimed membership-proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup are enforced before acceptance.

New passphrase_kdf backup envelopes below the unconditional base KDF floor (Argon2id memory_kib>=65536 / iterations>=3 / parallelism>=1; PBKDF2 iterations>=600000 with allowed digest_algorithm) MUST be rejected.
Key backup retrieval requires a session-bound unlock proof (ak.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1); any binding mismatch or bearer-token-only access fails closed before ciphertext is returned.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST publish fresh init key material, transition the old package to revoked with revocation_reason=keypackage_rotated, and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity, optionality, and profile gating: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported; high_security_organization and sovereign_deployment Realms MUST treat last-resort as forbidden even when the service supports the feature.

Cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim linearization and uncertain-outcome recovery: claim CAS, request ledger and serialized result commit atomically; same source/id/digest replays byte-identically; another digest conflicts without a second claim; query recovers the original outcome.

Peer KeyPackage claim requires both a participant signature bound to the exact request/service destination and the source-service HTTP Message Signature. Destination authority, contact, consent, capability, freshness and Direct Conversation no-last-resort gates fail closed behind one claim_failed surface without inventory leakage.

Concurrent Direct Conversation candidates may claim different single-use KeyPackages, but only the canonical binding winner activates Welcome and consumes; the loser Welcome is quarantined and its unconsumed claim expires to revoked, never published.
MIMI Provider Facade directory claims are accepted only when the Arkret profile and pinned MIMI Internet-Draft versions match.
ak.mimi.room_binding projects a MIMI room onto a Realm or Strand scope without making the MIMI room canonical truth.
MIMI key-material exchange maps to the Arkret KeyPackage claim lifecycle: the claimed package is single-use, becomes consumed after Welcome, and enumeration-sensitive failures share one public shape.
MIMI message/content ingress preserves the original envelope digest and MIMI message identity when mapping into Arkret events.
MIMI identifier queries use private-contact-discovery semantics and do not expose a raw contact graph or reachability proof.
MIMI consent state is isolated from Arkret Realm read/write capability grants.
MIMI proxy download obeys asset privacy policy and does not return direct object-store URLs when provider proxying is required.
Unsupported MIMI draft versions fail closed or require a new profile without silently mutating the v1 reducer profile.

Byte-level complete_control_state_v1 acquisition KAT and SDK verifier mutations for trust anchors, Seal paths and authority, chunk commitments, covered/state/frontier completeness, Event signatures and scope, governance roots, and commit binding fields.

Server materializer KAT that reconstructs the exact bounded four-chunk proof acquisition and returns no partial manifest for unreachable anchors, missing/forked/unverifiable source state, Bottom, visibility denial, or limit overflow.
Byte-level KAT for MLS ciphersuite 0x0001. The in-tree fixture pins the MLS WG corpus commit, every source-file SHA-256 digest, the ciphersuite selector, and fail-closed runner behavior.

Appeal verdict transitions are atomic: overturn requires a same-batch ak.moderation.decision.lift and never resurrects irreversible redaction/key-destruction effects; modify requires both a same-batch lift of the original decision and the replacement decision matched by modify_decision_ref.

E2EE franking proof construction, report submission, and moderator-side verification roundtrip per content-moderation.md section 3.4; digest mismatch or minimal-disclosure violations downgrade or reject the proof.

Multiple active moderation decisions use the deterministic strictest fold instead of being mislabeled as split; require_review is carried by the active decision add and resolution atomically lifts every applicable review gate before current authz is re-evaluated or a stricter replacement is added.

E2EE moderation evidence packages are encrypted to the authorized moderation recipient, target only reported events, carry reporter signature evidence, and reject MLS epoch/history secrets or unrelated plaintext.
Deterministic identity migration preserves every Morph field and canonical JSON value.

Deterministic ak.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ak.transform.rename.v1 rule renames a Morph field and leaves unrelated fields untouched; the post-migration fields projection is canonical-JSON byte-equal across replays.

Deterministic ak.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ak.transform.default_backfill.v1 rule backfills a new optional field with a fixed default while preserving existing fields; idempotent and replay-deterministic.
Deterministic integer-to-number schema widening preserves the JSON numeric value and rejects unregistered widening pairs.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
Expired policy decisions and decisions bound to an older auth/policy/membership frontier MUST be rejected on replay; receivers fail closed and re-request the policy check.
Receivers recompute the RFC 8785 JCS request_canonical_digest of the presented request body; mismatch with the signed bound_to transcript MUST reject the decision.

Explicit response closed loop with runtime addressed/self eligibility and restart dedupe gates, coordinator completion policy, causal request refs, controller validation, fail-closed non-echo handling, and controller-authored durable close control.

Event-fold and local-cache recovery: rebuild from accepted private history, causal folded-frontier validation, no Account Data merge, controller control ordering/sibling resolution, terminal absorption, reassignment, action-by-response-set mapping, and projection schema state invariants.

Containment: plaintext or shared-scope occurrences of exchange binding/control schema ids or exchange_id are hard rejects/invalid; publish output, Account Data, and public/shared surfaces carry no exchange material.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Production current-v1 protected endpoints MUST reject bare Authorization: Bearer unless it is bound by DPoP, an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature, detached JWS, mTLS, or equivalent sender-constrained proof; high-security profiles additionally require RFC 9421 PoP for regular writes / sensitive reads; a PoP signature whose created/expires falls outside the replay window MUST be rejected.

DPoP htu binds scheme, authority, and path: cross-authority/scheme reuse, untrusted forwarding headers, and missing authority are rejected; only a configured trusted proxy with scrubbed headers may reconstruct the external URI.
A DPoP/RFC 9421 grant-binding session key must not reuse bytes, fingerprints, thumbprints, or key identifiers from the long-term device identity key; reuse fails closed.

High-assurance snapshot inclusion-challenge sampling verifies sufficient event_id and actor_seq_range coverage, recomputes the event-set Merkle root, rejects commitment-root mismatch, and rejects silent actor sequence gaps.
Realm-scoped actor frontiers bind realm_id and actor_id, start at actor_seq 0, retain the complete sorted sibling head set, and hash the closed realm_actor transcript deterministically.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ak.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.
Receiver rejects sender_nonce_prefix collision or nonce prefix mismatch.
Receiver rejects repeated per-device AEAD nonce counter.
Receiver rejects pure random 96-bit nonce profile for v1 encrypted attachments.
mv_register join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
counter join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.

ordered_log per-issuer prefix from issuer_seq 0 and issuer equivocation convergence: byte-identical canonical projected write.op is idempotent, non-equivalent candidates for the same (cell, actor_id, issuer_seq) resolve to the greatest canonical event_digest compared as decoded octets, causal edges never change the winner, losers stay auditable, and digest collision fails closed.
fsm join: identical (from,to) sibling transitions converge idempotently; same-from different-to siblings return bottom (reject path).

A proposed Seal may include at most one mutually exclusive write to the same bottom=reject cell; apply_seal rejects a violating Seal, while unreachable Seal leaves retain ordinary bottom conflict semantics.

ordered_log issuer sub-chain seq gap yields contiguous_prefix plus pending_gap diagnostics; deterministic recompute after backfill. Equivocation winner selection belongs to ak.vector.lattice.ordered_log_join.v1.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

Accountability scope string/singleton-array and array permutations converge through a domain-separated canonical string-set digest before outer composite subject derivation; exact-set revocation remains isolated per cell.

RSVP derives a typed composite subject from payload event_ref, nullable occurrence, and the explicitly sourced envelope actor_id; causal successors dominate while concurrent mv_register heads remain exposed independently of HLC.

Calendar Strands activate exactly one way: Strand.schema_refs carries ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 and metadata.fields.calendar co-occurs in both directions on the post-patch object, the container self-schema is refused in schema_refs, legacy flat schedule fields and metadata.fields.profile/profile_refs impostors are refused, and writes bind the schema in requirements.schema[].

all_day selects the date branch and its negation the whole-second LocalDateTime branch for start, end and recurrence.until; intervals are half-open so end is strictly later than start; UTC timestamps, offsets, bracketed zones and fractional seconds are refused.

RFC 8984 subset defaults, base start as the first occurrence counted against count, implicit inheritance of base time and weekday components, count/until typing and exclusivity, by_* companion preconditions, and the paginated expansion with its candidate-period scan budget and revision-bound continuation.

Nonexistent and ambiguous local times both resolve with the offset in effect before the transition, so a fixed local meeting time does not drift across a DST boundary and the overlap emits exactly one occurrence.

Producers canonicalize Link aliases to the canonical Zone before signing, receivers refuse non-canonical signed zones, a schedule-signed tzdb_version outside the executable set fails closed, and a release bump may move derived instants without changing the signed timezone or any local occurrence key.
Excluded recurrence rules, recurrence overrides, RDATE/EXDATE, per-instance reschedule or cancellation, and the JSCalendar @type discriminator all fail closed instead of being silently ignored.

Identity-affecting schedule edits orphan instance RSVPs and mark series RSVPs needs_reconfirmation, non-calendar updates are not schedule revisions, divergent concurrent heads block RSVP until a resolution Event, and byte-identical concurrent heads settle without picking a winner.

ak.rsvp.set declares one deterministic reducer projection, set(payload.entry): an implementation that omits the registered write, projects an extra target, or derives a value different from the canonical payload entry fails conformance. Those writes are reducer-local output and never producer-selected Event fields.

Instance heads override series fallback without unioning them into a false conflict, causal successors dominate independently of arrival order and HLC, missing keys project encrypted_unresolved instead of a fabricated status, and equal decrypted plaintext is not a conflict merely because ciphertexts differ.

RSVP admission is capability-based rather than attendee-based, refuses cancelled events, and layers basis checks so that e2ee and plaintext Realms accept the identical canonical set: shape admission rejects without resolving anything, target admission reads only the referenced Events plaintext envelope and pends on dependency_missing, and basis validity is projection-only. It also fails closed above the 128-entry frontier bound and keeps missing, invisible, cross-Realm and non-calendar targets externally indistinguishable.

calendar.attendees is the single canonical roster: actor ids are unique, the omitted role defaults to required, at most one organizer exists, and roster membership creates no Realm or Circle membership and widens no history access.

One schedule patch derives exactly one notification per receiver over the pre/post roster union filtered by post-state access, mute, DND and push rules; encrypted schedules only produce the profile-defined blind wakeup; RSVP changes derive no schedule notification.

The RSVP response branch follows the effective scope encryption floor: plaintext is refused under an e2ee floor, permitted only with the declared rsvp_response data class otherwise, never silently downgraded, and the routing-visible metadata set is disclosed explicitly.

Realm Link FSM: all declared initial states and transitions are accepted, tombstoned is terminal except byte-equivalent replay, undeclared transitions reject with realm_link_invalid_transition, same-basis divergent siblings return bottom, general graph cycles remain valid, and self-reference rejects with realm_link_self_reference.

minimal-metadata and audited E2EE Realms force mention_routing_hint=disabled even when policy declares recipient_registered_token; no sidecar registration, comparison, or persistence occurs and delivery falls back to blind or batch wakeup.

ak.edge.push.command.notify returns one outcome per input device: every notification.devices[] device_id appears in outcomes[] exactly once, none missing, none duplicated, none unrequested, and a target-level failure is expanded per device instead of collapsing into a second response shape. accepted/duplicate forbid caller resend; only a rejected outcome carrying retry_after_ms, and only for the two registered caller-retryable reasons, transfers the next attempt to the caller. Provider delivery state, provider message ids and raw push tokens never appear in the response.

Account and events NDJSON stream trace conformance: catchup completion ordering, cursor-bearing frame closure, dropped-versus-resync branching, and reconnect position advancement are evaluated over complete traces rather than isolated frame schemas.

DeviceMessageEnvelope requires a sender-assigned message_id; unacknowledged byte-identical redelivery executes durable handler effects once, conflicting reuse fails with duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict, and distinct ids remain distinct logical messages.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.

Minimal-metadata author verification binds Event.actor_id and proof.verification_method to exactly one active MLS basic credential / LeafNode signature_key at the envelope epoch, rejects rollback/removal/duplicate/key-mismatch cases, and forbids principal-scoped keys/query fallback.
Audit binding is a closed control-plane FSM: active and suspended may transition as registered, revoked is terminal, and same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.
Audit session stages follow the registered request-authorize-notice-close FSM, permit explicit early close, reject skipped stages, and make close terminal.
Release recipient actor and public key must exactly match authorization and resolve to the same authorized audit actor; substitution fails closed.
Release is bounded by binding activation, first_auditable_epoch, encryption-time eligibility, sealed epoch state, and sealed_by_commit_ref.
Release requires an active binding, unexpired authorization, and accepted session head notice; suspended, revoked, expired, or wrong-stage inputs fail closed.
Same-basis close dominates release, earlier accepted releases must be frozen in close release_refs, post-close releases fail, and ordered_log ordering is deterministic.
Release material output is gated on accepted release plus a profile-valid RYW receipt, matching policy digest, and independent witnesses where attested hardware is claimed.
Byte-level RFC 9420 MLS-Exporter plus ExpandWithLabel KAT for the Arkret ak.history-v1 -> ak.content-v1 content-key chain, including domain/context/epoch negative mutations.
Canonical direct-conversation pair_key KAT over sorted stable subject DIDs and the Realm trust domain, including order-independence and unresolved-pairwise-DID rejection rules.
Direct Conversation Realm profile/discriminator bidirectional schema guard, MLS and closed-join shape, exact-two membership, no-Space policy and main-Strand invariants.
Authored active/retired binding facts and the participant-leave, Realm-terminal and main-Strand-terminal retirement boundary that forces fresh Realm, Strand and MLS identifiers.
Valid candidate filtering, causal supersession and unsigned-byte event_digest maximum selection for concurrent Direct Conversation bindings.
